solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feel acute embarrassment for the man supporting court order

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: a writ is an order issued by a court
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man squirms with shame while propping up a legal order.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm or twist with discomfort is the figurative sense of writhing in embarrassment.

clue.text: Hanger-on, one getting behind shelter

parts.note: a camp is a place of temporary shelter, tents or huts
someone who gets behind another is a follower

explanation.surface: A hanger-on is someone who ducks behind cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp follower was originally a civilian trailing an army, hence any hanger-on.

clue.text: Training regularly?

parts.note: read 'training' as travelling by train, and doing that regularly is the daily trip to and from work

explanation.definitionFit: Taking the train to work every day is the routine journey of an office worker.

clue.text: More than one course that is African sweetcorn

parts.note: a meal usually consists of several courses
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A multi-course dinner featuring maize from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one course' looks like a plural; it describes a single meal of several courses.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern Africa maize or corn on the cob is called by this local name.

clue.text: Ship's officer's instant true-life representation

definitions.note: the final 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: a representation is a new depiction, so the letters are presented in a different form

explanation.surface: A naval officer's snapshot portrait drawn from real life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges the fifteen letters of INSTANT TRUELIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior naval rank aboard a ship, second in command below the captain.

clue.text: I may be seen in 51 green assorted undies

indicators.note: the single letter is pictured appearing within the mixed letters

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A self-referring item spotted among fifty-one pieces of green underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' jumbles LIGREEN (LI plus GREEN); 'may be seen in' puts I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear in general is known by this French-derived word.

clue.text: Bouquet is old, that's grim

parts.note: dour means stern or grim

explanation.surface: A wine's bouquet described as aged and rather severe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but here it is the smell of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is a characteristic smell, especially of a wine, so a scent or smell.

clue.text: Proof of independent study clubs being held by the First Lady

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the name, enclosed by it

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
a den is a private study or room
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Evidence that a president's wife privately studies with golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' points at a president's wife but means Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is the material that proves or supports a claim, so it stands for proof.

clue.text: Dash! Old train service goes by ten

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway in Britain
IO looks like the digits 10

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an old railway service passing ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of verve or vigour is the same quality as lively spirit.

clue.text: Rush to get computers, etc, and scarper?

parts.note: to run is to rush
for means in order to get, as in going for something
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Dashing off to grab computer gear and then fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for fleeing, which is the idiom to make a dash and escape.

clue.text: Strung-out Louis must drop round for shot in the arm

indicators.note: strung-out suggests disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
drop tells the solver to remove a letter from the name

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An addicted man called Louis has to give up a session before getting his fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' takes O from LOUIS to leave LUIS; 'Strung-out' shuffles LUISMUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot in the arm is an idiom for a boost or incentive that spurs activity.

clue.text: Student starting late as breadwinner

indicators.note: the word begins later than usual, so its first letter is missing

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A trainee who began late ends up supporting the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadwinner earns money for a household, so is someone who brings in income.

clue.text: Top rep's book?

parts.note: read as the finest salesperson, then as a volume that sells in huge numbers

explanation.definitionFit: A title that sells in very large numbers is described as a chart-topping publication.

clue.text: Six-footer in religious group

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A tall man inside a religious cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it means a creature with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so a six-footer is a playful description.

clue.text: One after another

parts.note: the phrase normally means in sequence, but read as a person who comes after someone else

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows another in a post or role is the heir or replacement.

clue.text: Tenth speaker in musical story

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
read as ten, written IO like the digits 10, with the -th ending suggesting it comes at the end

explanation.surface: The tenth speaker appears in a sung narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenth' is read as 'ten' following the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale sacred musical work telling a story, usually biblical.

clue.text: More than one bird in negligee, seductively

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A bird dressed seductively in a negligee.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a common farmyard waterfowl, as one would expect from several birds.

clue.text: Produce family unit price

parts.note: a gene is a unit of heredity passed down in families
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A request to produce the price for a family.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce something is to bring it into being or create it.

clue.text: Capital of Puerto Rico's leaders with a visitor losing the way

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the two words
losing signals that letters are taken out

parts.note: a guest is a visitor
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Puerto Rico's chiefs and a lost visitor reach a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing the way' removes ST from GUEST, leaving GUE.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: High flier's suite?

parts.note: a high flier suggests a top executive's rooms, but read as a leaping ballet dancer's orchestral suite by Tchaikovsky

explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet suite of that name is danced by performers who leap high.

clue.text: Where a gangster traps US politician

indicators.note: the words around trap the letters, which lie concealed across them

explanation.surface: A gangster ensnares an American politician somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was a US president and Republican politician.

clue.text: Anger of jittery general when cut off at rear

indicators.note: jittery means nervous and shaky, so the letters are shaken up
the last letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A nervous general is angered when attacked from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off at rear' trims L from GENERAL; 'jittery' rearranges GENERA.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage is to make furious, the action of causing anger.

clue.text: Building not likely to move

definitions.meaning: a building where horses are kept
firm, steady and fixed in place

explanation.definitionFit: A horse's building and the adjective for something steady share the same spelling.

clue.text: Bear east, fleeing from Brunei in confusion

indicators.note: in confusion means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
fleeing from means a letter leaves the word

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A bear runs eastward away from Brunei in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E from BRUNEI leaves BRUNI, which 'in confusion' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a traditional folk name for a bear, from the Dutch for brown.

clue.text: Expressions of disbelief and surprise, going by island in boat

parts.note: no is an expression of disbelief
ah is an exclamation of surprise
Sark is one of the Channel Islands between England and France

explanation.surface: Gasps of amazement as a boat passes an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel built by the biblical patriarch to survive the flood was a boat.

clue.text: Commotion as noisily make tea with a laugh

indicators.note: noisily says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to brew is to make tea
ha-ha is a laugh

explanation.surface: Loudly brewing up and laughing causes a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Other ranks generally disheartened by revelry

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the enlisted soldiers

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Enlisted soldiers are generally downcast by partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' keeps only G and Y from GENERALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party marked by unrestrained revelry.

clue.text: Vocalist drunk on recent tour

indicators.note: drunk suggests the words are reeling, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A singer who was drunk on his latest tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A male alto or high-voiced male singer is a type of vocalist.
